_comment: Batch 13 (Sets 24-25). Distractor-only rewrites to remove the longest-answer cue. Correct options, stems, and rationales are unchanged; each distractor keeps its original meaning and stays wrong for the same reason. PN-S25-20 (weight-gain ranges) is in skipped.json as numeric.

RN-S24-01.B: A client with COPD who is requesting a scheduled bronchodilator inhaler that is due at the top of the next hour
RN-S24-01.C: A client with pneumonia whose temperature is 100.2°F (37.9°C) after a dose of antibiotics
RN-S24-01.D: A client with heart failure who is due for the daily weight and reports no new symptoms this morning

RN-S24-07.A: "Always use full sterile technique, with sterile gloves and a brand-new sterile catheter, every single time you catheterize yourself, even when you are at home by yourself."
RN-S24-07.C: "Catheterize only when you feel that you have to urinate, rather than on a schedule, so that you don't do it more often than you need to."
RN-S24-07.D: "Limit your fluids to about 500 mL a day so that you produce less urine and don't have to catheterize yourself as often during the day."

RN-S24-08.A: "Blow your nose gently several times a day to clear out any drainage or crusting that collects in your nose after the surgery."
RN-S24-08.C: "Brush your teeth vigorously starting right away so that the area around the incision stays clean."
RN-S24-08.D: "Drink all of your fluids through a straw so that you don't have to tip your head back or bend over."

RN-S24-09.A: "Trust the reading on your monitor and ignore your symptoms, since the sensor is more accurate than how you feel."
RN-S24-09.C: "Take a dose of your rapid-acting insulin now to bring your glucose back down into range."
RN-S24-09.D: "Remove the sensor and stop using it permanently, since it clearly isn't working correctly."

RN-S24-11.B: Loss of protein into the dialysate fluid
RN-S24-11.D: Too little fluid intake each day

RN-S24-13.A: Restrict the client's fluids to 1,000 mL per day to reduce the workload on the client's damaged kidneys
RN-S24-13.C: Encourage strict bed rest at all times to reduce the bone pain and protect the weakened bones from fractures
RN-S24-13.D: Increase the client's dietary calcium with milk, cheese, and yogurt at each meal to help strengthen the weakened bones

RN-S24-15.A: Tell the client firmly that the paralysis is fake, since all of the neurological tests have shown that nothing at all is physically wrong
RN-S24-15.C: Have staff force the client to stand and walk with assistance to prove to the client that the legs are able to move
RN-S24-15.D: Ignore the client and the reports of paralysis, since the workup has found no physical cause for the symptoms

RN-S24-16.C: A new viral infection such as influenza

RN-S24-17.A: "Take some acetaminophen and rest in a dark, quiet room until the headache and blurred vision go away."
RN-S24-17.C: "Headaches and blurred vision are normal after having a baby, because you're not getting very much sleep at night right now."
RN-S24-17.D: "Wait and mention the headache and vision changes to your provider at your 6-week postpartum checkup."

RN-S24-18.A: Normal progress in the active phase of labor
RN-S24-18.D: Supine hypotensive syndrome from lying flat

RN-S24-19.A: "Just watch for the battery to pass in your child's stool over the next few days, and call us back if it hasn't passed by then."
RN-S24-19.C: "Make your child vomit right away so that the battery comes back up before it can cause harm."
RN-S24-19.D: "Give your child a large meal with plenty of bread to help push the battery through the stomach quickly."

RN-S25-01.B: A client receiving IV iron sucrose who reports a metallic taste in the mouth and asks the nurse for a mint or hard candy
RN-S25-01.C: A client who is waiting in the lounge for a scheduled port flush and has no new complaints today
RN-S25-01.D: A client receiving IV hydration who feels chilly and asks the nurse for a warm blanket

RN-S25-02.A: Expose the infusion bag and tubing to bright light for several minutes to activate the medication before starting the infusion at the bedside
RN-S25-02.C: Give the nitroprusside as a rapid IV push through the closest port to lower the blood pressure quickly
RN-S25-02.D: Stop the infusion abruptly as soon as the BP returns to the normal range, without notifying the provider

RN-S25-03.A: "Metoprolol will raise your blood sugar to dangerous levels, so you will need to take much more insulin every day for as long as you're on this medication."
RN-S25-03.C: "Once you start the metoprolol, you can stop checking your blood sugar as often, since the medicine will keep your levels steady."
RN-S25-03.D: "Metoprolol protects you from low blood sugar, so you won't need to carry glucose tablets or snacks with you anymore when you go out."

RN-S25-04.A: "Take a dose of montelukast as your rescue medication whenever you have an asthma attack."
RN-S25-04.C: "You only need to take it on the days when you notice asthma symptoms such as wheezing."
RN-S25-04.D: "Montelukast replaces all of your other asthma medications, including your inhalers."

RN-S25-05.A: "Stop smoking completely on the day before you take your first dose, so that the medication can start working on your cravings right away."
RN-S25-05.C: "Take each dose of varenicline on an empty stomach, at least an hour before you eat breakfast or dinner."
RN-S25-05.D: "You can keep smoking as much as you like while taking varenicline, and the craving will simply go away on its own."

RN-S25-07.A: Lower blood glucose levels throughout the day, so the client's diabetes medications may need to be reduced while taking prednisone
RN-S25-07.C: No change in the client's blood glucose levels, so the usual monitoring schedule can continue unchanged
RN-S25-07.D: Stopping all of the client's diabetes medications until the course of prednisone has been completed

RN-S25-09.A: Dilute urine suggesting overhydration or fluid volume excess in the body
RN-S25-09.C: A normal finding in all situations that needs no follow-up
RN-S25-09.D: Evidence of diabetes insipidus with excessive urine output

RN-S25-11.A: Weight gain, cold intolerance, dry skin, hair thinning, and constant fatigue
RN-S25-11.C: Joint pain, mouth sores, and a butterfly-shaped rash across the face
RN-S25-11.D: Bloody diarrhea with crampy lower abdominal pain and urgency

RN-S25-12.A: Recommend an over-the-counter antidiarrheal such as loperamide and continue the next infusions as scheduled
RN-S25-12.C: Reassure the client that diarrhea is an expected and harmless effect of the treatment
RN-S25-12.D: Tell the client to stop drinking all fluids until the diarrhea and abdominal cramping have stopped

RN-S25-13.A: "Take each dose with a full glass of milk or a cup of yogurt to protect the lining of your stomach from irritation."
RN-S25-13.C: "Lie down flat right after you take each dose so that the medicine can settle in your stomach and you won't feel nauseated or dizzy afterward."
RN-S25-13.D: "Doxycycline is safe for children under 8 years old in all cases, so the rest of your family can take it too."

RN-S25-14.A: Increase the antipsychotic dose to help control the abnormal lip and tongue movements
RN-S25-14.C: Give benztropine as prescribed and expect the lip and tongue movements to resolve completely within a few days
RN-S25-14.D: Ignore the movements, since they are a harmless habit that develops after many years of treatment

RN-S25-15.A: Antipsychotics are the first-line treatment for all behaviors related to dementia, so the medication should be started right away, before trying any nonpharmacological approaches with the client
RN-S25-15.C: There are no special risks with antipsychotic medications in older adults with dementia, so quetiapine can be given in the same way it would be for a younger adult
RN-S25-15.D: The dose should be doubled right away if the agitation continues, because a higher dose will control the behavior more quickly and allow the client to rest

RN-S25-16.A: Caput succedaneum; no follow-up is needed, since it resolves in a few days
RN-S25-16.C: Normal molding of the skull bones from passing through the birth canal
RN-S25-16.D: Hydrocephalus with increased intracranial pressure and a bulging fontanel

RN-S25-19.A: Encourage the child to keep walking and playing sports so that the hip and thigh muscles get stronger
RN-S25-19.C: Apply a heating pad to the knee for 20 minutes several times a day to relieve the pain
RN-S25-19.D: Reassure the family that the pain is just growing pains, which are common at this age

RN-S25-24.A: Continue the infusion at the same rate and monitor the rash and the client's vital signs closely for changes
RN-S25-24.C: Permanently discontinue the acetylcysteine and document a drug allergy in the client's medical record
RN-S25-24.D: Administer epinephrine 0.3 mg IM into the thigh immediately and call the rapid response team

PN-S24-01.A: "Your child can stop using a booster seat at about age 5, once they have started kindergarten and are able to sit still for the whole car ride without slouching."
PN-S24-01.C: "Your child can stop using a booster seat as soon as they are able to buckle and unbuckle the seat belt without any help."
PN-S24-01.D: "Your child can stop using a booster seat once they weigh 40 pounds, no matter how tall they are or how the belt fits."

PN-S24-02.A: At about age 5, during the routine checkups before the child starts kindergarten
PN-S24-02.C: When all 20 baby teeth have come in, around age 3
PN-S24-02.D: Only if the child has tooth pain or a visible cavity

PN-S24-04.A: "Take away a favorite privilege or punish your child after each wet night so that they learn they need to stay dry."
PN-S24-04.C: "Wake your child up every hour throughout the night to walk them to the bathroom to urinate."
PN-S24-04.D: "Stop giving your child any fluids after lunch so that the bladder is completely empty by bedtime."

PN-S24-05.A: "Give your child antibiotics for 10 days to clear up the infection and the mouth sores."
PN-S24-05.C: "Give your child children's aspirin every 4 to 6 hours to ease the mouth pain and fever."
PN-S24-05.D: "This illness is not contagious, so your toddler can keep going to day care with the other children."

PN-S24-06.A: Restrict the resident's fluids during the day so that the resident needs to urinate less often
PN-S24-06.C: Insert an indwelling urinary catheter so that the resident stays dry and comfortable all day
PN-S24-06.D: Give sedatives at bedtime so that the resident sleeps through the night without getting up to use the bathroom

PN-S24-07.A: "You should ask your provider about starting a sleeping pill every night to help you sleep longer and more deeply."
PN-S24-07.C: "Waking up earlier and sleeping more lightly are often early signs of dementia, so you should be tested."
PN-S24-07.D: "You should nap for several hours each afternoon to make up for the sleep you're losing."

PN-S24-08.A: "That's only 800 mg of sodium, so you can safely eat the whole can today."
PN-S24-08.C: "Canned soup has no sodium, so it's a good choice for you."
PN-S24-08.D: "The number of servings doesn't matter, only the total calories."

PN-S24-09.A: "Stand up while showering so that you can move around and wash more easily."
PN-S24-09.C: "Complete all of your chores in the morning without breaks, while you have the most energy."
PN-S24-09.D: "Carry the heavy laundry baskets up the stairs quickly to finish the job sooner."

PN-S24-10.A: "Cover your mouth and cough into your bare hands, and then wipe them off on a tissue from the front desk."
PN-S24-10.C: "Sit close to the other clients so you don't miss your name being called."
PN-S24-10.D: "Remove your mask whenever you need to talk with the staff or other clients."

PN-S24-11.A: Raw vegetables with the skins on, nuts, and whole-grain bread
PN-S24-11.C: Bran cereal with dried fruit and milk
PN-S24-11.D: Popcorn, sunflower seeds, and fresh berries

PN-S24-12.A: Two slices of white toast with butter and a glass of orange juice
PN-S24-12.C: Scrambled eggs, bacon, and a slice of white toast
PN-S24-12.D: A glazed donut and a cup of coffee with cream

PN-S24-13.A: Performing the exchanges in the bathroom with the window and door open to let in plenty of fresh outside air
PN-S24-13.C: Warming each bag of dialysate in the microwave for a minute or two before the exchange
PN-S24-13.D: Skipping some of the scheduled exchanges on days when the client is feeling well and has energy

PN-S24-14.A: Gently pull and straighten the deformed arm back into normal alignment before applying a splint
PN-S24-14.C: Have the visitor move the injured arm through its full range of motion to test how serious the injury is before calling for help
PN-S24-14.D: Apply a heating pad to the injured forearm to relieve the pain and relax the muscles around it

PN-S24-15.A: "You can return to play at tomorrow's game as long as you feel fine when you wake up in the morning, even if you haven't been checked by a health care provider or the athletic trainer yet."
PN-S24-15.C: "Spend your time at home playing video games or watching screens for long periods, since that's a good way to rest your brain after a concussion."
PN-S24-15.D: "Take aspirin every 4 hours for your headache, and keep taking it every day until the headache and dizziness are completely gone."

PN-S24-16.A: "Bed bugs are known to spread serious diseases such as HIV and hepatitis, so you will need to be tested for these infections right away."
PN-S24-16.C: "Spray an insecticide directly on your skin and pillow before bed each night to keep the bed bugs from biting you."
PN-S24-16.D: "Bed bugs only live in dirty homes, so cleaning and vacuuming more often will get rid of them without any other treatment."

PN-S24-18.A: "Avoid all exercise during your pregnancy, since any kind of physical activity could harm your baby or cause you to have a miscarriage."
PN-S24-18.C: "Now is a great time to start a new high-intensity contact sport, such as kickboxing or competitive soccer, so that you stay in good shape for labor and delivery."
PN-S24-18.D: "Do all of your exercises while lying flat on your back, which is the safest position for you and your baby throughout pregnancy."

PN-S24-19.A: "Stop breastfeeding for a few days until the cramping goes away, and give your baby formula from a bottle instead until you're feeling better."
PN-S24-19.C: "Apply a heating pad directly to your perineum during each feeding to relax the muscles and ease the cramping."
PN-S24-19.D: "Strong cramping like this after delivery means that something is wrong, so you should go to the emergency room right away."

PN-S24-20.A: "The ointment helps prevent the yellow skin color of newborn jaundice during the first week."
PN-S24-20.C: "The ointment helps improve your baby's vision and eye focus during the first few weeks of life."
PN-S24-20.D: "The ointment helps prevent bleeding in your baby's eyes from the pressure of a vaginal birth."

PN-S24-21.A: Clean all of the residents' rooms and common surfaces with alcohol-based wipes only, since alcohol kills most viruses on contact
PN-S24-21.C: Allow staff members who are ill to keep working their scheduled shifts on the unit, as long as they wear surgical masks and wash their hands frequently during the shift
PN-S24-21.D: Use alcohol-based hand sanitizer instead of soap and water for all hand hygiene, since it is faster and kills most germs on contact

PN-S24-23.A: Keep the child isolated from friends and classmates to prevent infections during the hospital stay
PN-S24-23.C: Treat the child like a toddler and have the parents and staff make all of the decisions for them
PN-S24-23.D: Discourage the child from asking questions about treatment so that the child does not become frightened

PN-S24-24.A: Document that the resident is a picky eater who doesn't like the food
PN-S24-24.C: Switch the resident to a full liquid diet without obtaining an order so that eating is easier
PN-S24-24.D: Remove the dentures permanently so the resident can eat without them

PN-S25-01.A: "Test the bath water with your fingertips first, and if it feels hot to you, that's still fine for the baby's skin."
PN-S25-01.C: "Fill the tub with warm water up to the level of the baby's chest so that the baby stays nice and warm during the whole bath."
PN-S25-01.D: "It's okay to step away and leave the baby in the tub for a moment to grab a towel, as long as you hurry back."

PN-S25-02.A: "Baby walkers are a great idea, because they help babies learn to walk earlier and make their leg muscles stronger at the same time."
PN-S25-02.C: "Baby walkers are safe to use near the stairs, as long as you stay in the same room and keep an eye on your baby."
PN-S25-02.D: "Use the walker in the kitchen near the stove so that you can watch your baby while you cook dinner."

PN-S25-03.A: "You should never use a pacifier with a breastfed baby, because it will always cause problems with feeding and with your breast milk supply."
PN-S25-03.C: "Tie the pacifier to a ribbon around your baby's neck so that it doesn't fall out of the crib while your baby is asleep."
PN-S25-03.D: "Dip the pacifier in a little bit of honey first, so that your baby is more willing to take it at nap time and bedtime."

PN-S25-04.A: Vitamin C toxicity with diarrhea and cramps
PN-S25-04.C: Hypercalcemia only, from all of the calcium in the milk
PN-S25-04.D: Lactose intolerance with bloating and gas

PN-S25-06.A: "Use very hot water and soak for a full hour at a time so that you get the most benefit from each sitz bath."
PN-S25-06.C: "Add a capful of scented bubble bath to the water each time to make the sitz bath more relaxing."
PN-S25-06.D: "Stand up quickly as soon as you're finished, so that you don't start to get chilled in the bathroom."

PN-S25-07.A: Leave the warm compress in place overnight so that the area stays warm and the client doesn't have to be disturbed during sleep
PN-S25-07.C: Apply the warm compress directly over an area of active bleeding and leave it in place for 30 minutes
PN-S25-07.D: Have the client lie directly on top of the heating pad so that the heat reaches the deeper tissues

PN-S25-08.A: Take the oral temperature immediately while the client is sitting up and alert
PN-S25-08.C: Take it with the client's mouth open to let the heat escape
PN-S25-08.D: Take it right away and subtract 1 degree from the reading

PN-S25-10.A: The center of the heel, where the skin and fat pad are thickest
PN-S25-10.C: The back of the heel, just above the sole of the foot
PN-S25-10.D: The ball of the foot, just below the base of the big toe

PN-S25-11.A: Squeeze the urine out of a freshly wet disposable diaper into a sterile specimen cup
PN-S25-11.C: Give the infant large amounts of water first so that the infant voids sooner
PN-S25-11.D: Collect the urine from the bath water after the infant voids in the tub

PN-S25-12.A: Before entering the client's room, so that time is saved at the bedside
PN-S25-12.C: At the nurses' station after collecting specimens from several different clients
PN-S25-12.D: Leave it unlabeled, since the lab staff will label it when the specimen arrives in the department

PN-S25-14.A: Give the client a small glass of water to sip slowly, since a little water won't cause any harm before the surgery
PN-S25-14.C: Offer the client a piece of sugar-free hard candy to suck on until it's time for surgery
PN-S25-14.D: Tell the client that nothing can be done about the dry mouth until after the surgery is over

PN-S25-15.A: "You only need to change the water in the humidifier about once a month, and you can just keep topping it off with tap water in between."
PN-S25-15.C: "Add a small amount of household bleach to the water while the humidifier is running, so that the machine stays clean."
PN-S25-15.D: "There's never any need to clean a cool-mist humidifier, since the cold water inside doesn't allow germs to grow."

PN-S25-17.A: Offer the bedpan or the toilet only at times when the client says that they feel the urge to have a bowel movement during the day
PN-S25-17.C: Restrict the client's fluids and dietary fiber to reduce the number and size of the stools each day
PN-S25-17.D: Give the client a large-volume tap-water enema every day as the main part of the program for life

PN-S25-18.A: About 2 weeks after the last drink
PN-S25-18.C: Only after about 5 days without alcohol

PN-S25-19.A: "Give your child several instructions all at once, so that the chores and homework get done much faster each day."
PN-S25-19.C: "Remove all of the structure and schedules from your child's day so that there is less frustration."
PN-S25-19.D: "Punish every single mistake right away so that your child learns how to focus and pay attention."

PN-S25-21.A: The newborn's lips are tucked inward toward the gums, and there are clicking sounds and dimpled cheeks with each suck during the feeding
PN-S25-21.C: Only the tip of the nipple is in the newborn's mouth, and the baby feeds for just a few minutes
PN-S25-21.D: The mother reports sharp, pinching nipple pain that continues throughout the entire feeding

PN-S25-22.A: "Your baby is severely dehydrated from this weight loss and will need to be admitted to the hospital for IV fluids today."
PN-S25-22.C: "You'll need to switch your baby to formula immediately so that the weight comes back on."
PN-S25-22.D: "This weight loss means that breastfeeding has failed and isn't working for your baby."

PN-S25-23.A: A client with an ankle sprain from a fall that occurred about 2 hours ago
PN-S25-23.C: A client with a bruise on the thigh after a fall this morning
PN-S25-23.D: A client with facial swelling after dental surgery this morning
